headline: Apple alleges OpenAI destroyed evidence in ongoing trade secrets dispute
summary: Apple has surfaced forensic evidence from an ex-employee's MacBook in its legal case against OpenAI, with claims that OpenAI is actively destroying evidence related to alleged trade secret theft. Separately, OpenAI has restricted its Astra model citing critical cybersecurity risks and cut off AI access to SpaceX-owned Cursor, signaling internal governance tightening. For healthcare AI vendors and health system IT leaders, this signals that frontier AI companies face intensifying scrutiny around data handling practices and compliance obligations. The precedent being set in Apple's case could inform how regulators approach AI model training data provenance in regulated industries like healthcare, where data integrity and audit trails are non-negotiable. Health systems evaluating OpenAI partnerships should closely monitor these developments, as litigation outcomes may reshape third-party AI vendor contracts and data governance requirements.
